newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TACTICS FOR BAYERN MUNICH V VFB STUTTGART.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TACTICS FOR BAYERN MUNICH V VFB STUTTGART.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Bayern Munich and VfB Stuttgart who clash in the German first division on Saturday:

Playing style: On the surface, typically German with a libero, two out-and-out defenders at the back and versatile wing backs down the flanks who can defend and attack. But coach Giovanni Trapattoni, one of the great thinkers in the game, adds a few Italian touches to the tactics and Bayern are flexible.

Despite their array of stars they can play very defensively and look for the counter-attack, often to the frustration of leading striker Juergen Klinsmann. Veteran World Cup player Lothar Matthaeus normally operates as libero. Mario Basler orchestrates play in midfield.

Strengths: When they are on song, Bayern are attractive to watch. Basler has shown superb form recently. Klinsmann, playing his final few games for the club before he leaves for Sampdoria, has also looked sharp.

The club's main problem has always been controversy in the dressing rooms and Bayern can blow hot and cold. They can also play too defensively as they did in the corresponding match in Stuttgart earlier in the season.
Motivation: The German title is there for the taking. Bayern are desperate to win their third title of the 1990s and return to the lucrative Champions' League. The players need little motivating.

Possible line-up with shirt numbers: 1-Oliver Kahn, 10-Lothar Matthaeus, 5-Thomas Helmer, 2-Markus Babbel, 7-Mario Basler, 11-Marcel Witeczek, 7-Mehmet Scholl, 6-Christian Nerlinger, 17-Christian Ziege, 18-Juergen Klinsmann, 20-Ruggiero Rizzitelli.

Stuttgart look better going forward than defending. Their goalscoring has been remarkable this season with 72 goals to their credit and a goal difference of plus 38. Bulgarian Krasimir Balakov operates just behind the key striking pair of Fredi Bobic and Brazilian Giovane Elber. The trio have become known as the "magic triangle". Dutchman Frank Verlaat is an important figure at the back.
Strengths: Stuttgart's greatest strength is up front where talented Elber can turn a match in seconds and Euro 96 striker Bobic is an expert at poaching goals.
Motivation: A 60,000-plus crowd in Munich's Olympic stadium will provide an intense atmosphere for this south German derby. Stuttgart will not want to give the title to Bayern.

Probable line-up with shirt numbers: 1-Franz Wohlfahrt, 8-Marco Haber, 5-Frank Verlaat, 14-Thomas Schneider, 22-Andreas Buck, 12-Danny Schwarz, 10-Krasimir Balakov, 7-Matthias Hagner, 16-Gerhard Poschner, 9-Giovane Elber, 11-Fredi Bobic
